reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion: squared-off shoulder contour and severe pain after fall onto outstretched arm. 22M college wrestler presenting with right arm held abducted and externally rotated, loss of deltoid roundness, and subglenoid humeral head on AP X-ray.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion.
reference_soap.plan: Treat this as an urgent shoulder dislocation: document distal pulses, capillary refill, motor function, and axillary-nerve sensation before and after reduction; obtain appropriate pre- and post-reduction radiographs; provide analgesia/sedation and perform reduction only in a monitored setting by trained clinicians. Immobilize after successful reduction and arrange orthopedic follow-up for recurrent-instability risk. Escalate immediately for an absent pulse, worsening numbness/weakness, or suspected fracture.

teaching.diagnosis: Anterior shoulder dislocation with Bankart lesion
teaching.one_liner: 22M wrestler with a squared-off shoulder contour and severe pain after a fall onto an outstretched arm.
red_flags: Neurovascular compromise (axillary nerve) must be checked before and after reduction

must_ask.say: Can you describe exactly how you fell and what position your arm was in?

must_ask.objective: Assess the shoulder contour and position
must_ask.say: Does your shoulder look different, like squared off compared to the other side?

must_ask.objective: Screen for numbness over the shoulder (axillary nerve)
must_ask.say: Do you have any numbness over the outer part of your shoulder?
Has your shoulder ever popped out before?

must_ask.objective: Explain the reduction and post-reduction care
must_ask.say: Because this appears dislocated, trained clinicians need to reduce it urgently after checking blood flow and nerve function; those checks are repeated afterward, followed by a sling and follow-up.
